messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Admission Date: [redacted]
Discharge Date: [redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Principal Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented with severe right hypochondrium pain along with weight loss and alteration of general condition lasting for six months. The physical examination and laboratory examination were unremarkable. However, abdominal ultrasonography showed a 2.6 cm diameter intraluminal polypoid hyperechoic mass in the gallbladder. Computed tomography scan confirmed the presence of a gallbladder tumor that appeared as an enhancing pedunculated tumor without thickening of the gallbladder wall. A TDM scan showed a cortical fleshy nodule of the right kidney. 

The patient underwent an open cholecystectomy with a partial liver resection. The cholecystectomy specimen showed a metastatic renal cell carcinoma without any involvement of the gallbladder wall. A right radical nephrectomy was carried out through a right subcostal incision, and the histological study revealed a typical conventional clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

The patient was transferred to the department of Urology for further treatment. Following the nephrectomy, the patient recovered well with appropriate management of the surgical wounds.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:

None

Follow-up Plan:

The patient was advised to follow up with the department of Urology as per recommended schedule for a further course of treatment.	

Disposition:

The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this episode is clear cell renal cell carcinoma of the right kidney, whose gallbladder metastasis caused the presentation. Both the secondary deposit (cholecystectomy) and the primary (radical nephrectomy) were treated, so under the usual coding convention the primary renal malignancy is sequenced as principal. Malignant neoplasms fall in chapter C, and malignant neoplasm of kidney except renal pelvis is category C64.

CODE: C64
